title: Quenched activity induces nonuniversal scaling in nonreciprocal XY Models and surfaces
abstract: Active XY models and active surfaces are two paradigmatic nonequilibrium systems with distinct microscopic origins. We show that the hydrodynamic theories for a quenched-disordered nonreciprocal random bond two-dimensional XY model and an inversion-symmetric active surface tangentially advected by quenched velocities are identical. This theory predicts sub-logarithmic phase order in the XY model and sub- or super-logarithmic positional order in the surface for short-range disorder with nonuniversal exponents, which vary continuously with the degree of transversality of the disorder variance. We argue that the nonreciprocal random bond XY model can disorder through vortex proliferation.
summary: This paper demonstrates that the hydrodynamic description for a nonreciprocal XY model and an active surface advected by quenched disorder are mathematically identical. Using Renormalization Group theory, the authors predict that the resulting phase order is nonuniversal, depending continuously on the disorder characteristics. This provides a unified theoretical framework for studying non-equilibrium ordering in both condensed matter and active matter physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the scaling behavior and phase order in nonreciprocal, non-equilibrium systems by establishing an equivalence between two distinct physical models.
main_result: The theory predicts that both systems exhibit nonuniversal scaling exponents, allowing for phase order that can be stronger or weaker than the quasi-long-range order characteristic of the standard 2D XY model.
method: The analysis relies on deriving and analyzing a common hydrodynamic equation for both systems, followed by applying perturbative Dynamic Renormalization Group (RG) techniques.
model_or_system: The models include a 2D Nonreciprocal Random Bond XY Model (NRB XY model) and an active surface advected by quenched velocities. Both are governed by a continuum hydrodynamic equation involving spin stiffness, random disorder fields, and coupling constants.
key_observables: Phase order (XY model) and positional order (active surface); scaling exponents ($\eta, \eta_\kappa$); correlation functions $\langle|	heta(\mathbf{k}, t)|^2angle$.
important_parameters: Disorder variance transversality; coupling constants ($\kappa, \lambda$); disorder ratios ($\mu = D_T / D_L$).
main_assumptions: The derivation uses continuum limit approximations, assumes rotational invariance in 2D, and employs perturbative RG techniques.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the phase diagram in the $D_L - D_T$ plane mapping regions based on scaling exponents. Figure 2 illustrates the setup for both the 2D NRB XY model on a lattice and the active surface in the Monge gauge.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the equivalence between the microscopic dynamics of the XY model and the continuum equation for the active surface. It then uses continuum approximations and RG methods to calculate the scaling exponents and analyze the resulting phase transitions and ordering properties.
why_interesting: The connection between non-equilibrium active matter (surfaces) and classical statistical mechanics models (XY model) via a shared hydrodynamic equation is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium phase transitions in complex physical systems.
